summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted for evaluation of subjective fevers and chills two weeks after his recent transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for hepatocellular carcinoma. He remained afebrile during the hospitalization, and infectious workup—including blood and urine cultures and chest imaging—was negative, with findings most consistent with viral bronchitis. His right upper quadrant pain was attributed to post-TACE syndrome. A new resting tremor and cogwheeling in the right hand were identified and determined to be extrapyramidal side effects from prior use of prochlorperazine and metoclopramide, both of which were discontinued and added to his allergy list. He was started on diphenhydramine for tremor management and a lidocaine patch for localized pain. His chronic conditions, including alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis, hypertension, and ulcerative colitis, were maintained on existing regimens. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged in neurology, oncology, and transplant clinics.
problems: Bronchitis, not specified as acute or chronic
Unspecified extrapyramidal disease and abnormal movement disorder
Antiallergic and antiemetic drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
